judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the global search field in the header. The site's bundle.css sets ::placeholder color #d1d1d1, and the field background is white. Pixels in the screenshot confirm #d1d1d1 on #ffffff, which is 1.53:1 at 14px, well under 4.5:1. Understanding 1.4.3 states that the criterion applies to placeholder text. The placeholder "O que deseja encontrar?" is the only visible text in the field, since the legend "Busca global do Portal" is not shown, so no exception applies. The live CSS and HTML are the same as the capture.

judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: This is the icon-only AddToAny share link "Compartilhar no Twitter" (<i class="fa fa-twitter">). The live bundle.css sets .share-article li.twitter a{color:#55acee}, on the #f7f7f7 article background: 2.30:1, as claimed. The glyph is the Twitter bird in Twitter's brand blue, much as the Facebook icon uses #3b5998. Understanding 1.4.11 exempts brand logos shown in their brand colours under the essential exception, and says the exemption normatively carries over to a UI component, so I lean to a pass. Competent auditors would still reasonably disagree on whether a share-button glyph in a legacy brand colour is an exempt logo or a functional icon that needs 3:1. In the 1280px screenshot the floating chat button also covers most of this icon, a separate issue. The live CSS matches the capture.
